race/bowl: Here is a bowl: f of x equals x squared, lowest at zero. A ball at x equals one walks downhill by the gradient step: each move is minus eta, the step size, times the slope.
race/creep: With a small step size, eta at zero point zero five, the ball creeps.
race/slide: At zero point three, it slides straight in.
race/zig: At zero point eight, each step jumps past the bottom, but lands closer: the ball zigzags in.
race/blow: And at one point one, every jump lands farther out. The walk blows up.
race/why: Same bowl, same rule; only the step size changed. One number explains all four.
factor/a: To see why, give the bowl a steepness: f of x equals A x squared, where A is a positive number. Raise A, and the walls rise faster.
factor/grad: By the power rule, its gradient is two A x.
factor/step: So one step takes x to x, minus eta times two A x.
factor/pull: Both parts hold an x. Pull it out, and the step is x times one minus two A eta.
factor/name: So every step multiplies x by the same number, one minus two A eta: the step factor. It depends on the bowl and the step size, but not on where x is.
factor/num: With A at one and eta at zero point three, the factor is one minus zero point six, which is zero point four.
factor/x1: So from one, the first step lands at zero point four.
factor/x2: The next step multiplies by zero point four again, landing at zero point one six.
read/creep: Now the four walks. At zero point zero five, the factor is zero point nine: each step keeps ninety percent of x, so x creeps.
read/slide: At zero point three, it is zero point four: positive and well below one, so x keeps its sign and shrinks fast.
read/zig: At zero point eight, it is minus zero point six. A negative factor flips the sign of x: the jump to the other side.
read/zig2: But zero point six is less than one, so each landing is closer: x zigzags in.
read/blow: At one point one, it is minus one point two. The sign flips, and x grows every step: it blows up.
read/map: So the factor tells the walk. Between zero and one, x slides in, slower the nearer it is to one. Between minus one and zero, it zigzags in. Below minus one, it blows up.
try/p1: Try one: f of x is four x squared, x is three, and eta is zero point one. Where does one step land?
try/g: The gradient is two times four times three: twenty-four.
try/stp: The step is zero point one times that, which is two point four.
try/x1: Three minus two point four lands x at zero point six.
try/check: And after two steps? The factor here is one minus two times four times zero point one, which is zero point two.
try/two: So the second step multiplies zero point six by zero point two, landing at zero point one two.
try/where: And after that? The factor is between zero and one, well below one: x slides straight in.
